title: Adaptive footprint adapter for long‑context Llama/Mistral/Qwen
creator: Aisha Patel
description: Develop an adaptive 'footprint adapter' that reduces peak GPU memory for long‑context requests across Llama, Mistral, and Qwen model variants by dynamically remapping KV cache banks, applying lightweight lossy prefix compaction, and using sparse-KV compression heuristics. The adapter should be pluggable into the serving runtime so customers can enable per-deployment footprints without model code changes.
acceptance_criteria: Per-model configuration exists for Llama-2-70B, Mistral-8x, and Qwen-14 with long context >64k tokens
Peak GPU memory reduced by at least 18% on representative long‑context workloads (50k token sequences) compared to current baseline for each model family
95th percentile latency increase <= 8% for end-to-end single-request latency on P99 latency-sensitive routes
No correctness regressions: generation outputs for verification prompt sets must match baseline within existing quality metrics (BLEU/ROUGE-like evals and Redwood-defined hallucination checks)
Feature gated with config + rollout flag and integrated into console rollout controls
tasks: Design footprint adapter API and per-model profile schema
Implement KV bank remapper and in-place compaction pass
Add sparse compression layer and heuristic thresholds
Integrate adapter into continuous-batching fastpath and slowpath
Benchmark across target models on representative workloads
Add telemetry and expose per-route memory savings in Console
Write smoke tests, unit tests, and regression evals
Prepare rollout plan and feature flag
implementation_notes: Adapter strategy: keep KV layout compatible with runtime kernels to avoid per-step memcpy; use bank metadata to present a compacted logical view

Compaction approach: lightweight lossy prefix compaction only for non-reference tokens (drop sub-token prefixes that have low next-token entropy estimate), reversible at accessor level for correctness checks
Sparse compression: use 8-bit delta encoding for KV vectors where norm variance < threshold; fall back to raw storage when variance high
Memory reservation: reserve a small fallback slab per-GPU (configurable) for overflow to avoid OOM during abrupt working-set growth
Policy: per-model rolling thresholds (cold/warm/hot) based on observed per-route token distributions; allows tuning per-customer SLA
Compatibility: ensure adapter transparently supports quantized weights and existing quant-aware eviction heuristics
testing_plan: Unit tests for bank remapper correctness and edge cases (wrap/overflow)
Integration tests with continuous batching harness using synthetic traces (mix of short and long contexts)
Regression evals against existing quality test-suite (prompt sets for instruction-following and summarization)
Perf lab runs on dedicated GPU pools (A100 80GB and H100 80GB) with 3 seeds each
Chaos test: simulate sudden spike of long-context requests and verify no OOM and graceful fallback to reserved slab
rollout_plan: Feature gated behind runtime:footprint_adapter config flag
Start with internal canary on staging for non-critical accounts (1% traffic)
Expand to small set of production customers with long-context usage (via Dedicated and select Hosted routes)
Monitor memory savings dashboard and latency SLOs for 72h after each expansion step
Automated rollback trigger: memory regression >5% vs baseline or P95 latency regression >10%
